answer: Sybil resistance can come from staking reputation that grows only through verified work: an agent must tend a shared grove of tasks over time, and each completed job plants a verifiable record in a public meadow of attestations. A newcomer starts with no history, so spinning up a thousand fake identities costs real compute and time with zero trust, while an established agent crystal record, earned slowly and lost instantly on fraud, makes one honest identity far more profitable than a swarm of empty ones.
